edges.label: enables
edges.summary: BlitzBall reconceives run accumulation and wicket preservation as jointly optimizable objectives under a controlled-risk framework.
edges.context: BlitzBall, a tempo-maximization philosophy that reconceives the two objectives as jointly optimizable under a controlled-risk framework.

edges.summary: Momentum Windows is one of the six formal constructs that build the BlitzBall tempo-maximization philosophy.
edges.context: BlitzBall is built on six formal constructs: Momentum Windows, the Strike Pressure Index (SPI), Controlled Collapse Theory, Tempo Elasticity, Dynamic Run Velocity (DRV), and the Session Dominance Model (SDM).

edges.label: explains
edges.summary: Controlled Collapse Theory explains that apparent batting collapses under BlitzBall are consistent with rational risk-taking.
edges.context: via Controlled Collapse Theory, that a subset of apparent batting collapses under BlitzBall are statistically consistent with rational risk-taking rather than technical failure.

edges.label: related_to
edges.summary: Strike Pressure Index is related to previous work on pressure differential bowling analysis that predates the current session-level focus.
edges.context: Nakamura’s work on “pressure differential” bowling analysis [2] is the closest antecedent to our Strike Pres- sure Index

edges.label: related_to
edges.summary: Early session dominance scoring lacked the formal risk-budget allocation mechanism central to the current contribution.
edges.context: Okonkwo-Reyes [3] proposed an early version of session-level dominance scoring but did not incorporate a formal risk-budget allocation mechanism across ses- sion windows

edges.label: explains
edges.summary: Controlled Collapse Theory explains wicket clusters as expected outcomes of elevated risk budgets.
edges.context: Controlled Collapse Theory (Section III-D) reframes a subset of these clusters as statistically expected outcomes of elevated risk budgets rather than departures from normal batting be- havior.

edges.context: BlitzBall’s core operational rule is to escalate the risk budget (Section III-C) whenever M(Wk) > µthresh

edges.context: Teams and individual batters with Eρ > 1 are classified as tempo-elastic: capable of converting incremental risk-budget increases into disproportionate run-rate gains

edges.label: enables
edges.summary: Optimizing risk budget levels allows for greater tempo gains in match performance.
edges.context: Net win-probability gain relative to Orthodox-Attritional baseline peaked at ρ = 0.62

edges.label: part_of
edges.summary: Risk budget calibration is a component of the overall controlled risk strategy.
edges.context: Risk-Budget Calibration We swept the target risk budget ρ ∈ {0.30, 0.45, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.85} across a 150-match calibration subset.

edges.label: causes
edges.summary: Exceeding optimal risk levels leads to performance degradation due to wicket loss.
edges.context: performance degrading beyond ρ = 0.75 due to compounding wicket loss outweighing tempo gains on all but the flattest pitch conditions

edges.label: related_to
edges.summary: Baseline philosophies define how risk is applied across sessions.
edges.context: Orthodox-Attritional: uniform low-risk shot selection (ρ ≈0.22) with session-length wicket preservation as the primary objective

edges.label: explains
edges.summary: Balanced-Rotational philosophy applies risk without escalating during specific momentum periods.
edges.context: Balanced-Rotational: moderate risk budget (ρ ≈0.40) applied uniformly across sessions without momentum-window escalation

edges.label: enables
edges.summary: Adopting tempo instructions results in higher run rates.
edges.context: sides operating under BlitzBall recorded a mean run rate of 4.18 runs/over versus a pooled baseline mean of 3.02 runs/over

edges.label: enables
edges.summary: Explicit allocation of risk budgets across momentum windows leads to a substantially higher run rate.
edges.context: The results support Hypothesis H1: explicit risk-budget allocation across momentum windows generates a substantially higher run rate for a comparatively small increase in wickets lost

edges.label: part_of
edges.summary: Risk budgets are allocated across specific momentum windows within the framework.
edges.context: explicit risk-budget allocation across momentum windows generates a substantially higher run rate

edges.label: explains
edges.summary: Tempo elasticity measures the effect of individually calibrated risk budgets within the system.
edges.context: Opening batter Callum Drayce, deployed with an individually calibrated risk budget of ρ = 0.71, recorded a tempo elasticity of Eρ = 2.04
